title: Creating Lists
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to create lists with square brackets, including empty lists and lists that mix types.
learn: Create a list with square brackets
Lists can be empty or mix types
idea: You create a list with square brackets. Put commas between items: ["red", "blue"]. An empty list is just []. Useful when you will add items later. Lists can hold strings, numbers, and True/False together.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change scores = [10, 20, 30] to scores = [5, 15, 25]. Press Run. The second printed line should show those new numbers.

practice.text: Create a list of three school subjects and print it.
practice.hint: After the = sign, use square brackets and three subject names as strings, separated by commas.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if subjects is a list of three strings and the list is printed.

practice.text: Make an empty list called todos, then make a mixed list with a name, an age number, and True or False. Print both.
practice.hint: An empty list is just []. For profile, put a string, a number, and True or False inside one set of brackets.
practice.starterTip: Try todos = [] and profile = ["Alex", 11, True], then print(todos) and print(profile).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if todos is [] and profile mixes a string, a number, and a boolean; both are printed.

quiz.question: Which line correctly creates a list?
quiz.correct: Square brackets with commas create a list.

quiz.question: What is []?
quiz.correct: [] means a list with no items yet.
quiz.wrong: Empty square brackets make an empty list.

quiz.question: Can a list hold both a string and a number?

options.text: Only if you use curly braces

quiz.correct: Python lists can mix strings, numbers, and booleans.
quiz.wrong: Mixed lists like ["Sam", 11, True] are allowed.
